title: Why We Stay Silent About Mental Health?

seo_description: Khawar Shahzad and co-host Haris Sajid on why we stay silent about mental health: stigma, schools, social media, hasad and rashq, and safe spaces.
keywords: Why We Stay Silent About Mental Health

guest.name: Haris Sajid
bio: Haris Sajid is the regular co-host of Muffled Minds. Host Khawar Shahzad introduces him in this episode as one of his best friends, and says he did his bachelors in psychology.

In this episode Haris discusses with Khawar why we stay silent about mental health: the story behind Muffled Minds, the stigma around opening up, schools and institutes, social media, hasad and rashq, and the need for safe, judgment-free spaces.

summary: In the very first episode of Muffled Minds, host Khawar Shahzad sits down with his regular co-host Haris Sajid to tell the story behind the name: muffled means tangled minds, and the podcast is a platform where anxiety, depression and the things young people cannot say out loud finally get discussed. They start with the question everyone avoids: why do students in schools and colleges feel they cannot talk about their mental health, and why is sharing met with judgment or the label mental instead of support?

From there the conversation moves to where the silence comes from: parents and grandparents who never had the awareness or the words, schools and universities with no system and no psychologist to spot a struggling child, and a society that makes you ask what people will think before you ask for help. Social media makes it worse: you only see one side of the coin, compare your life with a celebrity's highlights, and sink into anxiety and depression over a struggle you never saw. The longest stretch is about hasad and rashq: hasad asks why he has it, rashq says mashallah and asks how I can get it too, and that keeda of improvement is what keeps you growing.

The last part turns to what to do instead of staying silent: pinpoint the problem early, teachers first and parents even closer, keep the chain from parents to teachers, and treat your children as friends so they can talk to you. The hosts are clear they are not perfect and no one can give a 100% solution, not even a psychologist, who can only show you the way. The episode closes with the difference between a psychologist and a psychiatrist, and the promise that the next episodes will bring real psychologists and the topics the audience asks for.

takeaways: Muffled means tangled minds: the podcast exists so anxiety and depression finally get discussed openly.
People stay silent because they fear judgment and the mental label, not because they have no problems.
A child who is never told about mental health grows up unable to ask for help, and parents who were never told cannot teach it.
Social media shows only one side of the coin: comparing your life with a celebrity's highlights hides their struggle and feeds anxiety.
Hasad asks why he has it; rashq says mashallah and asks how I can get it too, and that keeda is what drives improvement.
No one can give a 100% solution, not even a psychologist: he can show you the way, but you have to walk it yourself.
Pinpoint the problem early: teachers first, parents even closer, and keep the chain from parents to teachers.
Treat your children as friends and your parents as people you can talk to, so the barrier does not pass to the next generation.
